In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Fliessbach approach is not a general one, but a special case of the distorted wave Born approximation.
the renormalization kernels are of no practical importance in the description of transfer reactions.
the renormalization operator in the entrance channel is essential, whereas in the exit channel it is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conventional reduced width amplitude is a more natural and useful tool for the description of transfer reactions than the renormalized one.

renormalization operators, which are a consequence of antisymmetry, are important only for the description of structure, whereas the renormalization of the transfer form factor is due to reaction dynamics.
the renormalization kernels of Fliessbach are a special case, which is only valid for the special case of a single channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the renormalization operator in the exit channel is the most crucial ingredient for the description of transfer reaction data.
the renormalization kernels are determined by the structure of the initial and final nuclei, but not by the dynamics of transfer reaction.
the renormalization of the reduced widths is not a necessary consequence of antisymmetry but rather a result of the approximations used to calculate them.
